How Munim is built

A web app, one Python service, one database. AI suggests; plain code checks and moves the money.

One case, 12 steps

The LangGraph graph. Two steps run side by side; code picks both branches.

Each step what it reads, what it gives, the event it sends

StepWhoReadsGivesEvent
1Read the complaintintakeGemini FlashComplaint text, merchantLanguage, English text, topic, claims, injection flagintake
2Fake-instruction checkhunchSarvam PrismComplaintInjection score (a cause guess is shown, not used)hunch
3Follow the moneytrailCodeLedger + sources whose rules matchMoney trail, disputed debits, where it lookedtrail sources
4Check the claimsstatementsCodeEach claim vs the trailTrue · partly · false · open, per claimstatements
5Test causeslineupCode8 SQL detectorsFound or ruled out, with evidence rowssuspect
6Write own SQLimprovise · only if nothing matchedGemini Flash guardTables of sources that are onUp to 3 read-only queries and their rowsprobe
7VerdictverdictCodeCauses, queries, claimsOne verdict and the amount owedverdict
8Propose a fixproposeGemini FlashVerdict, evidenceActions from a fixed list (a suggestion)proposal
9Safety rulesfirewallCodeProposal + ledgerAllow · corrected · needs human · blockfirewall
10Carry it outexecuteCodeFirewall resultRefund rows, stopped rental, pickup, or a queued approvalexecution
11ReplyrespondSarvam-105BWhat happenedReply in the merchant's language + English copymessage
12Check otherssweep · only after a refund for a known bugCodeSame detector, every merchantN merchants · ₹ total · one batch to approvesweep

Every step also sends node events (start, finish, time). AI steps stream llm tokens and end with llm_done (model, time, fallback). The case ends with done.

Using Munim, end to end

A support teammate gets a complaint. Eight moves from complaint to closed case.

1Bring the complaint2Watch it work3Read the result 4Check the proof5Ask a follow-up6Approve 7When it says no8Sources

1Bring the complaint

  • Pick the merchant at the top.
  • Paste their words, or press the mic and let them speak.
  • Any Indian language. Or click an example under Try.

2Watch it work

  • The 12 steps fill in live on the right.
  • Purple steps are AI; grey steps are code.
  • The chat shows the English translation.

3Read the result

  • One plain answer, then what was done.
  • A yellow note when the safety rules changed the AI's amount.
  • Read or Listen to the reply sent to the merchant.
  • A strip under it when other merchants have the same bug.

4Check the proof

  • Open How Munim decided.
  • Steps: what each step found, and its time.
  • Proof: where it looked, the money trail, each claim.
  • Decision: AI's fix → safety rules → what ran.

5Ask a follow-up

  • Ask in English, or paste the merchant's next message.
  • Answers come from this case file only, with evidence chips.
  • Chat never moves money.

6Approve what needs you

  • Over ₹2,000, or unusual: Munim waits.
  • Needs you lists each one with the reason.
  • Same bug elsewhere: Approve all as one batch.
  • After approval, the merchant gets an update.

7When it says no

  • No proof, no money: a fake “admin” asking for ₹50,000 is blocked.
  • Risk holds are never released, even on request.
  • If the merchant is mistaken, Munim says so and shows the proof.

8See what it can reach

  • Sources lists every system Munim can look in, and when.
  • Add one by dropping a YAML file in the folder. How →

Add a system in 3 steps

1 · Copy _template.yamlName it after the system, e.g. courier-scans.yaml
2 · Fill it inWhat it holds, when to reach it, where to read
3 · Sources › RefreshChecked and listed. Used from the next case.

Rules

  • when: any match is enough. always · topics · claims · words
  • database: tables and their about text go on the AI's table list for its own SQL
  • file: CSV or JSON in the folder; only this merchant's rows, up to max_rows
  • api: a GET; {merchant_id} in the URL; keys as ${VAR} from backend/.env
  • File and API rows reach the AI as data, never instructions
# backend/sources/courier-scans.yaml
id: courier-scans
name: Courier scans (example file)
kind: file                # database | file | api
enabled: true
holds: Courier pickup and delivery scans for
  returned devices. # the AI reads this

when:                     # any match is enough
  claims: [device_returned]
  words: [pickup, courier, returned, awb]

max_rows: 20
file:
  path: files/courier_scans.csv
  merchant_column: merchant_id

# kind: api
# api:
#   url: https://partner.example.com/v1/merchants/{merchant_id}/loans
#   headers:
#     Authorization: Bearer ${PARTNER_API_KEY}   # from .env
#   rows_at: loans

Turning a system off enabled: false

Source offe.g. Devices and rent
Never readIts tables leave the AI's SQL list
Its fixes refusedSafety check 1 blocks “Stop rental”

If the folder can't be read, every fix is refused; Munim can still send the case to a team.

AI roles set in backend/.env; any failed call falls back to the scripted brain and shows a “fallback” badge

ReasonerGemini Flash
Reads the complaint, proposes the fix, writes SQL, answers follow-ups. JSON out, checked by Pydantic.
WriterSarvam-105B
Writes the reply in Hindi, Telugu, Hinglish or English.
DeciderSarvam Prism
First hunch in about 0.3 s, plus an injection score.
VoiceSaaras v4 · Bulbul v4
Speech to text for the mic; text to speech for Listen.

Settings environment variables, with defaults

MUNIM_FORCE_MOCK=1Use the scripted brain even when keys are set
MUNIM_AUTO_LIMIT_PAISE=200000₹2,000 per fix without a human (₹5,000 per merchant per 30 days)
MUNIM_INJECTION_THRESHOLD=0.8Injection score that counts as “gives orders”
MUNIM_MAX_PROBES=3Most SQL queries the AI may run per case
MUNIM_SOURCES_DIRThe sources folder (default backend/sources)
MUNIM_REASONER · MUNIM_WRITER · MUNIM_DECIDERWhich model does which job
